questions.stem: Who were the first three recipients of the Bharat Ratna in 1954?

options.option_text: Jawaharlal Nehru, Mahatma Gandhi, Sardar Patel
C. Rajagopalachari, Dr. S. Radhakrishnan, C. V. Raman
Rajendra Prasad, Lal Bahadur Shastri, B. R. Ambedkar
Subhas Chandra Bose, Mother Teresa, Morarji Desai

questions.explanation: The Bharat Ratna was instituted on 2 January 1954 by President Dr. Rajendra Prasad. The FIRST three awardees (1954) were: (1) C. Rajagopalachari — last Governor-General of India; (2) Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan — philosopher, later 2nd President; (3) Sir C. V. Raman — physicist, 1930 Nobel. Mahatma Gandhi never received the Bharat Ratna despite multiple nominations. Nehru received it in 1955 (in office — by himself, controversial). Sardar Patel was posthumously awarded in 1991. Dr. Ambedkar received it posthumously in 1990. NO BR between 1992-2008 due to an SC case challenging its 'medal' status (resolved by a 1995 judgment).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: In February 2024, the Government of India conferred Bharat Ratna on five personalities — an exceptional number. Which of the following was NOT among them?
questions.explanation: The five 2024 Bharat Ratnas announced Jan-Feb 2024 were: (1) KARPOORI THAKUR (posthumous — former Bihar CM, socialist leader); (2) L. K. ADVANI — former Deputy PM, BJP veteran; (3) CHAUDHARY CHARAN SINGH (posthumous — former PM, Jat leader); (4) P. V. NARASIMHA RAO (posthumous — former PM, architect of 1991 reforms); (5) M. S. SWAMINATHAN (posthumous — Father of India's Green Revolution, agricultural scientist). The most Bharat Ratnas announced in a single year. Manmohan Singh (10th PM, architect of 1991 reforms as FM) was NOT awarded (and passed away Dec 2024). Total Bharat Ratnas to date: 53.

questions.stem: How many Nobel Prizes have been won by persons of Indian origin or Indian citizens, and who was the FIRST?

options.option_text: 9 total (5 Indian citizens + 4 OCI/foreign-naturalised); Rabindranath Tagore 1913 (Literature)

questions.explanation: Indians/Indian-origin Nobel Laureates (9 total): (1) Rabindranath TAGORE — Lit 1913 — FIRST Asian Nobel Laureate; (2) C.V. RAMAN — Physics 1930 — Raman Effect; (3) Hargobind KHORANA — Medicine 1968 — genetic code (born India, then US citizen); (4) MOTHER TERESA — Peace 1979 — Indian citizen; (5) Subrahmanyan CHANDRASEKHAR — Physics 1983 — stellar structure (born Lahore undivided India, US citizen); (6) Amartya SEN — Econ 1998 — welfare economics; (7) V. RAMAKRISHNAN — Chem 2009 — ribosome (born Chidambaram, US/UK citizen); (8) Kailash SATYARTHI — Peace 2014 — child rights; (9) Abhijit BANERJEE — Econ 2019 — poverty experiments (born Kolkata, US citizen). V. S. Naipaul (Lit 2001, Trinidad-born Indian origin) is sometimes counted as 10th.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The Jnanpith Award, India's highest literary award, is given by whom and for writing in which languages?

options.option_text: Bharatiya Jnanpith Trust; 22 scheduled languages + English
Indian Council for Cultural Relations; any Indian language

questions.explanation: The Jnanpith Award is instituted by the Bharatiya Jnanpith Trust (established 1944 by the Sahu Jain family), given annually since 1965 for literary work in any of the 22 Scheduled Languages + English. Prize: ₹11 lakh + bronze Saraswati statue + citation. First recipient: G. Sankara Kurup (Malayalam, 1965). First woman: Ashapoorna Devi (Bengali, 1976). First in English: Amitav Ghosh (2018). Odia didn't have a Jnanpith winner till 1973 (Gopinath Mohanty). Hindi has most winners. Distinct from Sahitya Akademi awards (which are by genre in each language each year). Saraswati Samman is another major literary award (KK Birla Foundation since 1991).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The Dadasaheb Phalke Award for lifetime achievement in Indian cinema is named after whom?

options.option_text: The first Indian to win an Oscar

questions.explanation: Dhundiraj Govind Phalke (1870-1944), known as 'Dadasaheb' Phalke, is regarded as the Father of Indian Cinema. He directed India's FIRST feature film RAJA HARISHCHANDRA (1913, silent, black-and-white) — the actual release was on 3 May 1913 at Coronation Cinematograph, Mumbai. He made 95 films and 27 shorts. The Dadasaheb Phalke Award was instituted in 1969 (his birth centenary year); first recipient: Devika Rani. Prize: Swarna Kamal (Golden Lotus), ₹10 lakh, shawl. National Film Awards are separately given. India's national cinema day: 3 May. who made India's first feature film 'Raja Harishchandra' (1913).

questions.stem: Which Indian-origin scientist won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2009 for his work on the structure and function of the ribosome?
questions.explanation: Venkatraman 'Venki' Ramakrishnan (born 1952, Chidambaram, Tamil Nadu; US/UK citizen) won the 2009 Chemistry Nobel (shared with Thomas A. Steitz and Ada E. Yonath) 'for studies of the structure and function of the ribosome'. Served as President of the Royal Society, UK (2015-20). Khorana won Medicine 1968 (genetic code); Chandrasekhar won Physics 1983 (stellar structure — Chandrasekhar limit); Banerjee won Economics 2019 (poverty experiments, with Esther Duflo and Michael Kremer). Tagore (Literature 1913), Raman (Physics 1930), Mother Teresa (Peace 1979), Sen (Economics 1998), Satyarthi (Peace 2014) complete the list of Indian-linked Nobels.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The Magsaysay Award is often called the 'Asian Nobel Prize'. It is named after a former President of which country?
questions.explanation: Named after Ramon Magsaysay, the 7th President of the Philippines (1953-57), who died in an air crash 1957. The Award was instituted in 1957 by the Rockefeller Brothers Fund to honour his memory. Given since 1958 in categories like government service, public service, community leadership, journalism/literature/creative arts, international understanding, emergent leadership. Indian recipients include: Vinoba Bhave (1958, first Indian), Mother Teresa (1962, pre-Nobel), Satyajit Ray (1967), Ela Bhatt, Baba Amte, Mahasweta Devi, Kiran Bedi, Arvind Kejriwal, TM Krishna, Bezwada Wilson, Anshu Gupta, Ravish Kumar (2019 last Indian so far). The Emergent Leadership category was discontinued in 2020; 2020-21 awards skipped due to COVID.

questions.stem: The Param Vir Chakra (PVC) is India's highest military gallantry award. Who was the FIRST recipient, posthumously awarded?
questions.explanation: The Param Vir Chakra (PVC) was instituted on 26 January 1950, retrospectively effective from 15 August 1947. The first PVC was awarded POSTHUMOUSLY to Major Somnath Sharma (4th Battalion, Kumaon Regiment) for his leadership in the Battle of Badgam (3 November 1947) during the First Kashmir War. Only 21 PVCs have been awarded (14 posthumous). Other notable recipients: Major Shaitan Singh (Rezang La 1962), Lance Naik Albert Ekka (1971), Second Lt Arun Khetarpal (1971), Capt Vikram Batra (Kargil 1999), Capt Manoj Pandey (Kargil 1999). India's second-highest military honour is Maha Vir Chakra (MVC), third is Vir Chakra. In PEACETIME, the corresponding highest is Ashoka Chakra.

questions.stem: The Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna (India's highest sporting honour) was originally known as what, and is given by which ministry?

options.option_text: Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna; Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports
Dronacharya Award; Ministry of Home Affairs
National Sports Award; Ministry of Education

questions.explanation: Originally the 'Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna' (instituted 1991-92), RENAMED in August 2021 to 'MAJOR DHYAN CHAND KHEL RATNA AWARD' (after the legendary hockey player and 3-time Olympic gold medalist, 1928/1932/1936). First Khel Ratna awardee: Viswanathan Anand (1991-92). Given by the Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports. National Sports Awards hierarchy: (1) Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna (top, for outstanding performance over 4 years); (2) Arjuna Award (consistent excellence for 4 years); (3) Dronacharya Award (for coaches); (4) Dhyan Chand Award (for lifetime contribution — different from Khel Ratna). Awarded every year on 29 August (National Sports Day, Dhyan Chand's birthday).
